Meta’s Data Center Robots: Tugger Carts and Laundry Folds
Meta is putting robots to work in data centers. One folds laundry. One moves racks.

Meta has been experimenting with robotics inside its data centers since at least 2023. A YouTube video from that year showed a self-driving tugger robot moving heavy server racks and a wheeled, barcode-reading robot tracking inventory. Meanwhile, Watney, launched in 2023, demoed a laundry-folding robot it claimed could also handle janitorial work. The push suggests a convergence of logistics automation and facility maintenance. Whether these demos translate to reliable, large-scale deployment remains the open question for the next phase of infrastructure scaling.

NVIDIA and Apple Unveil Compact AI Computers for Robots
New hardware prioritizes reliability and bandwidth over raw speed.

At Computex 2026, Jensen stated that performance per watt, reliability, and long lifetime are the core features of future GPUs. This focus shifts attention from benchmark peaks to sustained operational stability. NVIDIA and AMD have published results on larger models such as DeepSeek V4 Pro and Kimi K3, using AgentX. The infrastructure supports this by ensuring that for every XPU, 1.6Tb/s of global bandwidth will travel to the global switch tray over the copper backplane. These compact units aim to deliver generational gains by solving the thermal and connectivity bottlenecks that plague current deployments.

From Atari to EVE: 15 Years of AI Game Research Explained
DeepMind traces its game AI lineage from Pong to No Man's Sky.

A new DeepMind blog post maps fifteen years of research, showing how general learning algorithms evolved from mastering simple Atari classics like Breakout and Space Invaders to navigating complex 3D environments. The work highlights a shift from game-specific engineering to systems that achieve human-like play across diverse titles such as Valheim and Hydroneer, culminating in the legacy of AlphaGo’s 2016 victory over Lee Sae Dol. This retrospective clarifies that modern capabilities are built on incremental breakthroughs rather than sudden magic, offering a grounded view of where game AI stands today without hype or doom.

Agent control is becoming an operations discipline
Google DeepMind is replacing “keep an eye on the agent” with coverage, recall, and time-to-response.

Google DeepMind's AI Control Roadmap treats agent oversight as measurable operations: trusted systems supervise working agents, interventions can block harmful actions, and teams track monitoring coverage, detection recall, and response time. MARA calls the metrics more important than another safety adjective. DOT likes that control finally has service-level indicators, but asks for their cost. REX warns that supervising visible reasoning will age quickly as agents become more opaque. The quiet race is now between agent capability and the observability stack meant to contain it.
